# Optimistic stock deduction

> A cheap stock look-up before charging, then a guarded `UPDATE "Product"` after charging that only succeeds if enough stock is left, so the shop never oversells.

_Part of [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md)_

Inside `PaymentService.executePayment`, stock is checked twice. First comes a plain `SELECT quantity FROM "Product"`. If the product is missing or has too little stock, the service sends a [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](charging-a-payment.md) through the outbox and returns the payment. No Stripe call is made. This check is only a shortcut to avoid a pointless charge and refund. It does not stop two buyers racing. The real guard comes after Stripe says the charge `succeeded`. Inside the finalize transaction, one `UPDATE "Product"` subtracts the quantity, adds 1 to `version`, and only matches rows where `quantity >= :quantity`. The service reads the row count. If it is 0, someone else took the stock first. In that case the function returns early with `needsRefund: true`. The payment stays `PENDING`, and no ledger entry is written. After the transaction ends, the service refunds the charge. This follows [Refund when stock runs out after charging](refund-saga.md). If the update matched a row, the normal path continues: update the payment status, then record the sale in the ledger. See [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md) for the whole flow.

**Look at:** [`PaymentService.executePayment` in payment.service.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/application/payment.service.ts#L65)

## Pieces

- Cheap stock pre-check before charging: A plain `SELECT quantity` on `Product` that stops early with [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](charging-a-payment.md) when stock is missing or too low, so no Stripe charge is made.
- [Guarded stock update after a successful charge](guarded-stock-update.md): An `UPDATE "Product"` that subtracts the quantity, bumps `version`, and matches only when `quantity >= :quantity`. A row count of 0 means the stock was lost.
- Insufficient stock error sent to the caller: [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](charging-a-payment.md) is a business error sent through the outbox. It is used with two messages: one for the pre-check, and one saying the stock ran out after payment and the buyer was refunded.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| database | `Product` | Read for `quantity` in the pre-check. Then updated to subtract the quantity and increase `version` after a successful charge. |
| database | `Payment` | Stays `PENDING` when stock is lost, then is set to `REFUNDED` after the refund. |
| external | `Stripe` | The charge happens between the two checks. A refund is issued if the guarded update matches no row. |
| queue | `Outbox (``OutboxService.notify``)` | Carries [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](charging-a-payment.md) back to the caller, both when the pre-check fails and after a refund. |

## Also relies on

- [Charging a card through Stripe](charging-a-payment.md): The stock checks are steps inside the payment flow that charges the card and records the result.

## Watch out

- The pre-check gives no safety on its own. Two buyers can both pass it, and only the guarded `UPDATE` decides who gets the stock.
- Stock is deducted only after Stripe has already charged the card. Losing the race therefore means a charge followed by a refund.
- When the guarded update matches no row, the function returns before the `Payment` is touched, so it stays `PENDING` until the refund step marks it `REFUNDED`.
- The pre-check failure returns the payment without calling Stripe, and [`Domain_InsufficientStockError`](charging-a-payment.md) goes to the caller via the outbox rather than to a dead-letter queue.
